text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA
- Opposition coalition Zajedno (Together) presidential council clears mistrust, coalition to stay together.

- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic calls for urgent republican parliament session to discuss problematic conduct of Montenegro's state security service which he says "threatened constitutionally guaranteed human rights and freedoms".

- According to Nasa Borba sources, Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic at closed session of the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) of Montenegro leadership refuses to replace state security service chief Vukasin Maras.

- Former Yugoslav prime minister, U.S. businessman Milan Panic, is the best man to resolve Serbia's biggest problem, poverty and unemployment, followed by Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic, according to a public opinion poll.

- Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce industry committee says heavy tractors should be produced in the country. Serbia needs around 200 heavy tractors to prepare for fall sowing and local industry is not equipped to supply them in time, experts say.
- Rehabilitation of banks in Serbia implies rehabilitation of problematic firms whose debts should also be converted into state stakes.
- Businessman Bogoljub Karic says he will run for president of Serbia if elections are regular, expects 70-80 percent of Kosovo Albanians to vote for him if they turn out in elections.
POLITIKA
- Serbian government adopts measures to revive production in metal complex, additional tax reductions for firms.
- More than 90 percent turnout of Serbs in elections in Eastern Slavonia, Croatia.
- UNTAES spokesman Philip Arnold blames Croatian government for "inadequate and incomplete support for elections in Eastern Slavonia".
- McDonalds fast food chain to open new restaurant in southern Serbian city of Nis by the end of April.
- Dinar picks up on the black market to 3.6 dinars to the German mark compared to 3.7 early last week.
- Zastava Cars adopts new production programme for 1997. Of 22,250 cars planned by year end, 10,000 to be exported.
- Democratic Party proposes new law against smoking due to increase in malignant lung diseases.
- Montenegro's ruling DPS discusses reconstruction of republican government behind closed doors.
- Yugoslav Left vice president Aleksandar Vulin says conflict in the Montenegrin leadership is the internal affair of the DPS.
- Serbian Agriculture Minister Jovan Babovic says Serbia has potential for $2 billion worth of food exports this year.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- New Yugoslav passports will not begin being issued as of Tuesday because of delays in printing.
- Agenda of Serbian parliament session to include election of president and members of republican election commission.
- No official confirmation about a rumoured visit by an International Monetary Fund delegation to Yugoslavia in May. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
